I have some experience with OCR. I like to convert old books into EPUB. People think OCR is perfect, it's not. It works well with a perfect font, perfectly aligned, not tilted in the image, with no smudges or ink smears. If the page is not perfectly square in the image, OCR has trouble. It also has trouble with really old fonts, like from the 1600s (yes, I've tried to OCR those too). It has trouble with fancy fonts, bad spacing, and often ligatures (like where 'li' is combined into a single character 'li'). You can forget trying to OCR a latin bible due to the fancy fonts they wrote in.

To throw off OCR, make the font fancy, like script, or gothic. Give it a shadow. Add extra space here and there. Misspell words on purpose.
